chunks: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī and Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Goods were brought to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام from Miṣr, so he prepared food and invited the merchants for it. They said, “We will take it at dah dawāzdah.” Then he said:
They said, “For every ten thousand, two thousand.” He said:
“Then I will sell you these goods for twelve thousand.”

key_terms.أَبِيعُكُمْ: I sell to you, expressing the act of sale
key_terms.أَلْفَيْنِ: two thousand, the added amount mentioned by the merchants
key_terms.التُّجَّارَ: the merchants invited for the transaction
key_terms.بِاثْنَيْ عَشَرَ أَلْفًا: for twelve thousand, the final stated sale price
key_terms.عَشَرَةِ آلَافٍ: ten thousand, the base amount in the pricing formula
key_terms.مَتَاعٌ: trade goods or merchandise being sold
key_terms.مِصْرٍ: Egypt, the place from which the goods arrived

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام conduct a sale with merchants when pricing goods?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a commercial exchange involving Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and a group of merchants concerning goods brought from Miṣr. It reflects a sale discussion in which the price term was clarified and then stated plainly as twelve thousand, making it relevant to trade and financial dealings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3800 - Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi and Muhammad al-Halabi narrated from Abu Abdullah (as):

Goods arrived for Abu Abdullah (as) from Egypt. Imam (as) prepared food and invited the merchants.
They said: "We will take it at dah dawazdah (a price of twelve)."
Imam (as) asked: "And how much does that amount to?"
They replied: "For every ten thousand, two thousand more."
Imam (as) said: "Then I will sell you these goods for twelve thousand."
